paper_metadata.title: Impact of vanadium (V) content on in-situ oxidation, high temperature mechanical strength and tribological properties of Al0.5CrFeNiVx high entropy alloys

evidence.quote: four vanadium (V) containing high entropy alloys (HEAs) Al0.5CrFeNiVx (x = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0) were developed and investigated
The mechanical properties of cast Al0.5CrFeNiVx HEAs were investigated utilizing Vickers hardness testing, nanoindentation, and compression testing.

This analysis reveals the complexity and variability of wear mechanisms in Al0.5CrFeNiVx HEAs at high temperatures, and also reveals the correlation between high temperature oxidation and high temperature wear and friction.

process_steps.input_state: commercial Al, Cr, Fe, Ni, and V pellets with 99.5 wt.% purity

evidence.quote: bulk Al0.5CrFeNiVx (x = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1) HEA specimens wear fabricated through the traditional arc-melting method, utilizing the commercial Al, Cr, Fe, Ni and V pellets with their purities of 99.5 % (weight percent) as initial material. The melting process was conducted in an argon gas protecting atmosphere. Each ingot had a total weight of approximately 70 g and was repetitively melted at least five times to confirm the chemical homogeneity.

Using wire electrical discharge machining (EDM), as-cast HEA ingots were cut into samples measuring 8 × 3 × 15 mm3 for high temperature sliding wear tests, cylindrical samples with a diameter of 6 mm and height of 9 mm for Gleeble compression testing [65], as well as samples for characterizing phase compositions, microstructures, and hardness.

These changes in lattice parameters indicate the solid solution strengthening effect caused by vanadium solute atoms.
This structural transition increases the alloy hardness and compressive strength through solid solution strengthening, precipitation strengthening and grain refinement strengthening.
This structural transition increases the alloy hardness and compressive strength through solid solution strengthening, precipitation strengthening and grain refinement strengthening.
solid solution strengthening: vanadium atoms cause lattice distortion when they substitute into the BCC lattice because they are larger than the matrix atoms
precipitation hardening: formation of the Laves phase (VAl2) introduced at higher vanadium contents caused random distribution of intermetallic precipitates within the matrix
grain refinement strengthening: vanadium addition refines the grain structure by inhibiting grain growth during solidification and increases the number and area of grain boundaries

Such a microstructure change enhanced the solid solution strengthening and improved the mechanical strength (such as hardness and compressive strength) by increasing the lattice distortion and refining grain structures of these Al0.5CrFeNiVx HEAs.
The thicker and more stratified oxide layer in V0.75 also indicates a higher degree of oxidative wear, likely due to the combined effects of high temperature and the specific alloy composition.

For V1.0, the lack of layering in the friction film suggests a more homogeneous wear process, but the presence of vanadium and chromium oxides in the outer layer and a plastically deformed inner layer indicates significant oxidative and adhesive wear mechanisms.

When sliding wear temperature is above 600 °C, molten vanadium oxide forms during repetitive frictional contact between HEA disc and Si3N4 ball, resulting into lubricious molten wear thus reducing the friction coefficient and wear rate of Al0.5CrFeNiVx HEAs [65].

For all four vanadium contents, abrasive wear and plastic deformation dominate during sliding wear at RT due to the direct asperity contact and repetitive shearing between the alloy and frictional counterface, associated by mild oxidation wear [34,66,83].
